steps: Open Obsidian TEST vault with roam-workspace enabled.
Run command Open Journal Stream.
Observe the main editor leaf.
evidence: Main editor contains one daily-note-editor-view backed by Journal V2 and no temporary journal-v2-view leaf.
View state has selectionMode=folder, target=Journal, timeField=journalDate, selectedRange=recent-30.
After progressive scrolling reaches the end, fixture files 260812.md and 2026-08-11.md are both present in the rendered list in date order, with no pending cards.

steps: Open plugin settings for Journal Stream.
Change journalFolder, defaultOpenMode, initialRange, enableExportMarkdown.
Return to an already open Journal Stream view.
evidence: Settings controls render without overlap.
Settings no longer expose a Legacy/V2 engine selector or migration rollout control.
Copy Journal stream as Markdown command availability matches enableExportMarkdown.
Temporary settings persist to data.json and cleanup restores the original bytes exactly.
cleanup: Restore default settings used by the PRD.

steps: Open Journal Stream.
Require the exact registered fixture Journal/_journal_stream_regression_fixture/260812.md; fail closed if it is absent.
Focus that fixture's persistent embedded editor and record its mount ID, geometry, and Properties state.
Append a runId-bound unique marker to the fixture through the embedded editor.
Wait for Obsidian save.
Exercise preview, expanded Properties, re-edit, and final preview using the same mounted editor.
In an unconditional cleanup transaction, restore the original source, embedded editor buffer, and Properties state.
evidence: The exact runId-bound marker reaches a larger source file through the embedded editor save path.
All edit/preview stages and post-cleanup state retain one editor mount ID with at most 1px geometry delta.
Cleanup is attempted even after a failed UI step and proves source bytes and embedded editor buffer exactly match the original.
The marker is absent from source and editor after cleanup, and the original Properties collapsed state is restored.

steps: Open Journal Stream.
Ensure at least one fixture card is visible.
Trigger Copy Journal Stream as Markdown from the command palette.
evidence: Clipboard contains # Journal Stream Export.
Clipboard includes source_path and date_source for visible fixture files.
Copy failed state is not shown for successful copy.

steps: Open Journal Stream with 260812.md mounted in the embedded editor.
Modify 260812.md externally outside the embedded editor.
Observe the card state.
evidence: Card auto-syncs from the external Markdown source.
No conflict/reload prompt is shown for ordinary external source changes.
The embedded editor reloads from the Markdown truth source.

steps: Open Journal Stream.
Rename fixture 260812.md to 260812-renamed.png.
Rename it back to 260812.md.
Rename an adjacent non-Markdown file to 260814.md inside the fixture directory.
evidence: Renamed .md to non-Markdown disappears from the Journal Stream.
Renamed file returning to .md appears again when it matches the source and range.
New Markdown rename enters the list without duplicating cards.

steps: Open Journal Stream.
Inspect bad-yaml-260813.md and unparsed-fixture.md cards.
evidence: Bad YAML does not break the whole view.
Unparsed file shows fallback metadata instead of crashing.
Other fixture cards remain editable.

steps: Warm and reopen the matching Journal workspace leaf for the 100-file / 1k-entry fixture.
Warm and reopen the matching Journal workspace leaf for the 2k-file / 20k-entry fixture.
Modify one mounted Medium fixture source 20 times through Vault.modify and observe the embedded editor.
evidence: Small warm open <= 200ms and the first persistent editor is ready.
Medium warm open <= 500ms and progressive DOM remains bounded.
Single-file modify-to-UI p95 <= 300ms.
Measurement method, Obsidian version, viewport, all 20 samples, and source restoration are recorded.
